project: Remove Dashboard Session Hook Re-exports From Public
description: Narrow `features/dashboard/public` to a screen-only app composition boundary by removing dead `DashboardSessionProvider` and `useDashboardSession` re-exports, keeping dashboard session behavior unchanged, and proving the boundary with behavioral tests instead of export inventories.

context.customerAsk: Remove dead session-provider hook re-exports from `ui/src/features/dashboard/public/index.ts` so the dashboard public barrel exposes only `DashboardScreen`, matching how `App.tsx` and app stories already consume it, without changing dashboard session behavior.
context.problem: After stream/timeline hook splits and session scope context landed, production code imports session symbols from `dashboard/session/dashboard-session-provider` directly, but `dashboard/public` still relays `DashboardSessionProvider` and `useDashboardSession` even though no maintained consumer imports them from the public barrel—widening the surface and inviting incorrect cross-feature coupling.
context.solution: Delete the session hook re-exports from `dashboard/public`, keep screen-only forwarding from `dashboard-screen`, retarget any stragglers to the session module, and add or retain behavioral smoke (public-barrel render of `DashboardScreen`, existing app-shell tests) so session-scoped dashboard composition still works without export-list assertions.

acceptanceCriteria: `ui/src/features/dashboard/public/index.ts` exports only the intended dashboard screen public surface; `DashboardSessionProvider` and `useDashboardSession` are not re-exported from the barrel.
Every maintained import from `features/dashboard/public` in `ui/` is screen-related (`DashboardScreen` with current app and Storybook consumers).
Dashboard session selection, pause, and stream/snapshot behavior remain unchanged in automated regression coverage.
Behavioral smoke renders `DashboardScreen` from the public barrel and asserts an observable dashboard shell outcome with active session context.
No export-name inventory test is added as the primary proof of the narrowed public surface.
Focused dashboard and app-shell tests pass after the boundary change.
Quality gate: UI typecheck, `bun run lint`, and relevant tests pass before merge.

userStories.title: Screen-only dashboard public barrel
userStories.description: As an app composer, I want `features/dashboard/public` to expose only `DashboardScreen` so cross-feature imports do not pull session internals through a compatibility barrel.
acceptanceCriteria: `ui/src/features/dashboard/public/index.ts` removes named re-exports of `DashboardSessionProvider` and `useDashboardSession` and keeps screen-only forwarding from `../components/dashboard-screen`.
`DashboardScreen` remains importable from `features/dashboard/public` with the same props and runtime behavior as before.
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Dashboard public import boundary
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want all consumers of `features/dashboard/public` to import only screen symbols so session scope stays on `dashboard/session/dashboard-session-provider`.
acceptanceCriteria: No file under `ui/` imports `DashboardSessionProvider` or `useDashboardSession` from `features/dashboard/public`.

Imports from `features/dashboard/public` in `App.tsx` and app-level Storybook stories remain `DashboardScreen` only; any straggler is retargeted to `features/dashboard/session/dashboard-session-provider`.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Behavioral smoke for public-barrel dashboard composition
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want regression tests that prove `DashboardScreen` from the public barrel still renders a working session-scoped dashboard shell without asserting export inventories.
acceptanceCriteria: A focused test imports `DashboardScreen` from `features/dashboard/public`, renders it with existing dashboard test providers/fixtures, and asserts an observable shell outcome (for example loading status, header, or session tab chrome).
Any pre-existing public-barrel test that only asserted session relay export names is removed or replaced by this behavioral smoke; export-name lists are not the primary acceptance mechanism.
Existing app-shell and `DashboardScreen` tests continue to pass without session-behavior regressions.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: an app-level Storybook story importing `DashboardScreen` from `features/dashboard/public` renders the dashboard shell.
